status_summary: As of 2026-10-07 the record is mixed. Funding for several Mandate programs is in place: the July 2025 reconciliation law (P.L. 119-21, Sec. 20008, Enhancement of resources for nuclear forces) gave SLCM-N 2 billion dollars plus 400 million for its warhead (per CRS) and the B-21 about 4.5 billion dollars for production capacity (per Air & Space Forces Magazine), and the FY2027 request (testimony of 2026-04-30) seeks 71.4 billion dollars for the triad, including 4.6 billion for Sentinel, 6.1 billion for the B-21, about 1.5 billion for LRSO and 16.2 billion for Columbia-class. Schedules for the headline items run later than the Mandate asks: Sentinel was restructured with initial capability in the early 2030s and some Minuteman III missiles expected to serve into the 2050s (against the Mandate's call to reject further life extensions), statute sets SLCM-N limited operational deployment by September 2032 (FY2026 NDAA, P.L. 119-60, Sec. 1633) and initial operational capability by September 2034 (FY2024 NDAA) rather than the end of the decade, and Los Alamos says its working plan for 30 pits per year is 2028, not the 2026 date in a 2019 law. On testing, CRS (version of 2025-12-16) reports that the President made statements in October and November 2025 suggesting the United States could restart nuclear testing and that it is unclear whether any policy change will follow; per a Wikipedia summary the Energy Secretary said in November 2025 that explosive testing would not resume, and per a senator's press release he told senators on 2026-05-13 that reliability does not require it; CRS puts U.S. readiness to resume testing at 24 to 36 months from a presidential decision, and no explosive test or date was found. For FY2027, the House passed its defense authorization bill (H.R. 8800) 216 to 212 on 2026-07-22 (House Clerk roll call 278). The Senate Armed Services Committee voted 18 to 9 on 2026-06-10 to report its bill, S. 4784, which was reported on 2026-06-15 (per CRS); cloture on the motion to proceed failed 50 to 46 on 2026-07-14 (Senate vote 195), and CRS showed neither bill enacted as of 2026-09-01. CSIS reported on 2026-08-18 that neither FY2027 defense appropriations bill had been enacted and that each chamber had passed a continuing resolution at FY2026 levels. On or about 2026-10-01 news reported that the National Nuclear Security Administration had concluded a subsurface, non-nuclear chemical high-explosive experiment at the Nevada site to improve detection of low-yield nuclear explosions; this was not a nuclear explosive test, and no nuclear explosive test or test date was found.

timeline.event: Reconciliation law P.L. 119-21 is enacted; its Sec. 20008 is titled Enhancement of resources for nuclear forces. A CRS report says it provides 2 billion dollars to accelerate the SLCM-N missile and 400 million dollars for its warhead; Air & Space Forces Magazine reports it gave the B-21 about 4.5 billion dollars for production capacity.

A CRS In Focus on U.S. nuclear weapons tests (version of 2025-12-16) reports that the President made statements in October and November 2025 suggesting the United States could restart nuclear testing, that it is unclear whether any policy change will follow, that the U.S. aims to be able to resume testing within 24 to 36 months of a presidential decision, and that the U.S. has observed a moratorium on explosive testing since 1992; the Energy Secretary's November 2025 remark that explosive testing would not resume is known only from a Wikipedia summary.

The FY2026 NDAA becomes law as P.L. 119-60 (approval date 2025-12-18 per the govinfo.gov editorial note); its table of contents lists Sec. 1633 (matters relating to the nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile), Sec. 1641 (strategy to sustain Minuteman III and maximize end-of-life margin) and Sec. 3112 (plutonium pit production capacity). A CRS report of 2026-01-08 says the Act authorizes 210 million dollars for the SLCM-N missile and 50 million for the warhead and directs a limited number of assets for limited operational deployment by September 2032; a separate FY2024 NDAA provision requires initial operating capability by 2034.

A CRS In Focus on the nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile (IF12084, version of 2026-01-08) summarizes P.L. 119-21 funding (2 billion dollars for the missile, 400 million for its warhead) and the NDAA authorizations and deadlines.

House passes the FY2026 defense spending package: Sentinel 2.65 billion dollars with added oversight, B-21 net cut of 211 million, LRSO cut by about 217 million. An arms-control center fact sheet later lists FY2026 enacted levels for these programs, which indicates the package became law, but the enactment date was not retrieved.

ExchangeMonitor reports the Los Alamos director saying the lab exceeded its pit production objectives over the past year (pit counts are classified) and that its working plan targets 30 pits per year in 2028, versus the 2026 goal in a 2019 NDAA provision; the Savannah River plutonium facility is not expected online until the mid-2030s.

Sentinel commanders brief that new modular silos replace silo reuse (about 450 needed), a prototype silo is under construction in Utah, a test launch is planned for 2027, initial capability is expected in the early 2030s (the program once targeted 2029), restructuring should finish by end of 2026, and some Minuteman III missiles will serve into the 2050s. Defense News reported the early-2030s timeline on 2026-02-17.

In testimony to the Senate Armed Services Committee, the Secretary of War presents a FY2027 request with 71.4 billion dollars to modernize the triad: 6.1 billion for the B-21 (at least 100 planned), 4.6 billion for Sentinel (400 deployed missiles, 450 silos), about 1.5 billion for LRSO and 16.2 billion for Columbia-class (a fourth boat and continued work on the third). The article does not address SLCM-N, NNSA or pit production.

At a Senate Armed Services hearing, Energy Secretary Chris Wright says the decision on an explosive nuclear test rests with the President and that explosive testing is not needed to assure weapon reliability, per a senator's press release; no administration decision to test is reported.

An advocacy group's summary (a lead, not stage-deciding) says it authorizes Sentinel at the 4.6 billion dollar request, B-21 at 6.1 billion, and 250 million dollars for SLCM-N against a zero request.

The statement came on the preceding Wednesday (inference: 2026-09-30); the experiment date was not given.

title: Accelerate nuclear modernization, expand the deterrent, and restore test readiness
uncertainties: The Energy Secretary's November 2025 response still rests on a Wikipedia summary; CRS IF11662 (2025-12-16) confirms the October and November 2025 presidential statements and the 24 to 36 month readiness figure, but the presidential post itself and any written directive were not found. The 2026-05-13 account of Wright's testimony comes from a Democratic senator's press release (the hearing record was not read), and the same office's April 2026 release gives no test-readiness timeline. The enacted laws were checked only through their tables of contents on govinfo.gov (P.L. 119-21 Sec. 20008; P.L. 119-60 Secs. 1633, 1641 and 3112), not the section text; the funding amounts and dates come from CRS IF12084 and the FY2027 figures from a Department of War article. The Arms Control Center and Arms Control Association (advocacy sources, used as leads only) report different groupings, for example a zero discretionary SLCM-N request for FY2027 versus a five-year projection, and an expected summer 2026 Sentinel cost estimate that I could not confirm was released. B-21 and Sentinel comparisons across years are affected by one-time reconciliation money in FY2026. Not researched: nuclear-capable F-35, warhead life-extension schedules (W80-4, W87-1, B61-12), Columbia-class delivery dates, and any nuclear testing or SLCM-N developments after mid-May 2026. The title of P.L. 119-60 Sec. 1641 (a strategy to sustain Minuteman III and maximize end-of-life margin) bears on the Mandate's call to reject further life extensions, but its text was not read. Searches run: SLCM-N status; nuclear testing at the Nevada site 2026; NNSA pit production 2026; FY2027 nuclear budget request; presidential nuclear testing directive (CRS). Freshness pass 2026-10-12: FY2027 authorization and appropriations were not enacted as of the latest sources (CRS update of 2026-09-01, CSIS of 2026-08-18); whether a continuing resolution became law by 2026-10-01 was not confirmed. House passage and the failed Senate cloture vote were confirmed on the House Clerk and Senate roll call pages; the committee vote and report dates rest on CRS through a mirror site. The Sentinel Milestone B decision and new cost estimate (projected by end of 2026 per Defense News, February 2026) were not found. The authorization levels for Sentinel, B-21 and SLCM-N come from an advocacy group's summary of the committee bill and are not used for the stage. The October 2026 Nevada experiment is reported by one local news outlet; the NNSA statement itself was not read, and its date is inferred.
